sn36.6:1.25: The ablative _dukkhasmā_ here is explained by the commentary as taking an instrumental sense, like the preceding terms.
sn36.6:4.2: The text seems to require an implicit “mental”. It is perhaps corrupt, as “learned” does not really fit here, since letting go attachment to feelings requires spiritual realization; the commentary explains “learned” as “learned in scholarship and in realization”. It’s also syntactically curious, as all three terms in this line end in _-pi_, which normally connects items in a set, but here _sukhampi dukkhampi_ belong together but _bahussutopi_ belongs with _sapañño_ in the previous line.
